images.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: conceptual infographic for a Chinese technical blog article about PPO, DPO, GRPO.
Primary request: create a polished, accurate comparison diagram, landscape 3:2. Match the site's existing educational diagrams: pure white background, crisp flat vector-like rounded rectangular cards with thin colored borders, very pale blue/amber/green fills, black connecting arrows, dark navy sans-serif typography, generous whitespace, restrained simple line icons. No photographic elements, no shadows, no gradient, no watermark.
Title verbatim: "PPO · DPO · GRPO"
Subtitle verbatim: "Three ways to improve a policy"
Composition: three stacked horizontal lanes, each with a large algorithm label at left and exactly three connected boxes from left to right. PPO lane blue; DPO lane amber; GRPO lane green. Big readable English labels, no equations or Chinese.
PPO lane: "Rollouts + rewards" → "Critic → advantages" → "Clipped policy update".
DPO lane: "Chosen / rejected" → "Policy vs reference" → "Preference loss".
GRPO lane: "Same prompt × G" → "Group-relative advantages" → "Clipped policy + KL".
Each lane has a short note below its boxes: PPO "Learned value baseline"; DPO "Offline preference pairs"; GRPO "No learned critic".
A separate bottom strip contains exactly: "old policy: sampling snapshot     reference policy: fixed anchor".
Accuracy: these are separate methods, do not connect the three lanes together, do not imply DPO uses rollouts or a critic. GRPO is the original outcome-supervised formulation. Keep all text verbatim and sharply legible. Simple sample-sheet/checkmark/group icons may supplement labels. This is a conceptual explanation, no empirical charts or numeric performance claims.

Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: conceptual teaching infographic for a PPO / DPO / GRPO blog article.
Primary request: show how rewards within ONE prompt become GRPO advantages, using an exact four-answer example. Landscape 3:2. Match educational diagrams in the same blog: white background, flat rounded panels with thin blue green amber purple outlines, pale pastel fills, dark navy bold sans-serif English labels, clear dark arrows, generous whitespace. Large readable typography, simple line icons. No photography, watermark, empirical plot, dense formulas or decorative background.
Title verbatim: "GRPO: Compare Within One Prompt"
Top: one small blue card "One prompt", which branches to exactly four equal answer cards in a row, labelled "Answer 1", "Answer 2", "Answer 3", "Answer 4".
Below those cards aligned columns show a row labelled "Reward" with values exactly "0", "0", "1", "1".
Then a full-width pale purple normalization strip: "Group mean = 0.5     Population std = 0.5".
Below aligned with the same four answers, a row labelled "Advantage" has values exactly "-1", "-1", "+1", "+1". Negative values in amber, positive values in green. At the right or beneath: "Ignoring numerical epsilon".
Below the advantages, a short label: "Relative signal for the policy update".
Bottom separate pale neutral card, title "Equal rewards". It contains exactly "1, 1, 1, 1  →  0, 0, 0, 0" and subtitle "Zero reward-driven advantage; KL can still contribute".
Footer verbatim: "Normalize each prompt separately".
Accuracy: exactly four answers and precisely corresponding values, never mix prompts, population standard deviation is 0.5 for [0,0,1,1]. Equal rewards produce zero advantages, not necessarily zero total gradient. Avoid implying a direct guaranteed increase in individual token probability. No extra mathematical symbols or formulas.
